Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ptetools 1.1.0

  • New check_overlap() reports overlap diagnostics for each group-time cell (#28). It uses the same cells and covariates as pte_default(). For each cell it gives the share of treated units outside the comparison group’s covariate range (including the lagged outcome with lagged_outcome_cov = TRUE) and, where it can be estimated, the share with a propensity score above 0.9 and 0.999. Shares are reported weighted too when weightsname is given.

  • pte_attgt() (used by pte_default()) warns more usefully:

    • When it switches from AIPW to regression adjustment, the warning now says why: too few treated units for the number of covariates, or propensity scores near 1 for a given share of treated units (it used to say “small group size” either way).
    • It now warns when it drops a covariate that does not vary among comparison units but does among treated units, such as a dummy for a region with treated units only. The estimates then extrapolate for those treated units. Dropping covariates that are redundant for treated units too (duplicates, empty factor levels) stays silent.
    • Each kind of warning is given once per call, listing the group-time cells (in the original group and period codes) instead of once per cell, and not again for every empirical bootstrap draw.

  • New unsupported_covariates() flags, for each predicted unit, the covariates that were dropped for collinearity in the fitting sample but matter for that unit’s prediction (#34). It is the check behind pte_attgt()’s dropped-covariate warning, exported so that other attgt_funs can apply the same rule.

  • New pte_cell_warning() lets any attgt_fun report problems this way: pte() collects the warnings across group-time cells and reports each kind once, listing the cells.

  • pte() (e.g. pte_default()) with boot_type = "empirical" no longer warns “aggte_fun not specified” for ATT results, where the default aggregation is the only built-in one. The warning remains for QTT and QOTT results.

  • Bug fix: uniform confidence bands for QTT curves (and QTT minus ATT) could be absurdly wide when the outcome has a mass point, such as zero earnings (#33). The critical value standardized the bootstrap draws by an IQR-based scale, but the band multiplied it by the bootstrap SD. At quantiles inside the mass point the IQR scale is nearly, but not exactly, 0, so the critical value exploded. Both now use the SD, and quantiles whose draws never vary are left out of the critical value. Standard errors are unchanged.

  • Bug fix: with time periods coded 2, …, T (for example 2:3 or 2:5), results were not mapped back from the internal coding 1, …, T. Group-time results were labeled with the wrong groups and periods, and the overall ATT and event study were NaN. Whether to map back was guessed from whether the internal periods were all valid original periods; it now checks whether the setup function recoded them. Periods coded 1, …, T, calendar years and other codings were unaffected.

  • Bug fix: standard errors and uniform bands for ATT(d) from process_dose_gt() (used by contdid) were wrong with a not-yet-treated comparison group, the default. The comparison-group part of the influence function had the wrong sign. That cancels within a single group-time cell, but not across cells where the same unit is first a comparison unit and later treated. In simulations, 95% intervals covered about 92%; they now cover 95%. Results with never-treated comparisons, and those for ACRT(d) and the overall parameters, are unaffected.

  • Bug fix: with repeated cross sections (panel = FALSE), standard errors of the event study and the overall ATT left out the term for estimating the group shares used to weight ATT(g,t) (#32). They now match did::aggte() exactly, with and without sampling weights. The difference was small in practice (about 0.01% on mpdta); group-time standard errors were unaffected.

  • Bug fix: the empirical bootstrap ignored sampling weights. Each draw was set up again without weightsname, so every draw was unweighted and weighted standard errors and bands were those of the unweighted estimator (#21). This affected every estimator using boot_type = "empirical" with weights, including QTT runs and qte’s estimators. Point estimates were correct. The QOTT bootstrap also rebuilt its draws without ret_quantile, so its standard errors were for the median whatever quantile was estimated.

  • Sampling weights audit (#21): did_attgt() and covid_attgt() now use sampling weights (they did not pass them to DRDID), and setup_pte_basic() gains weightsname (it set every weight to 1). Weighted estimates and standard errors from pte_default() match did::att_gt() for panel data (ATT(g,t), event study and overall, both estimation methods, with covariates, both base periods and comparison groups, and with clustering) and for repeated cross sections (ATT(g,t)), and are unchanged when the weights are rescaled.

  • Bug fix: aggregated QTTs and QOTTs mixed the wrong cells’ distributions. attgt_pte_aggregations() returned its weight vectors in the order of an internal table that merge() sorts by group, while the cells’ F0/F1 are in the order the cells were computed. With more than one group, the overall, event-time and group QTTs could put weight on pre-treatment cells and none on some post-treatment cells. Cells dropped as NA also shifted later weights. The weights now follow the order of the cells. ATT results were not affected. Found while adding the ATT to QTT runs (#27).

  • QTT runs (gt_type = "qtt" with qtt_pte_aggregations()) now also return the ATT, from the same cells, weights and bootstrap draws (#27): $att holds the overall, event-time and group ATTs with standard errors and confidence intervals, and $qtt_minus_att holds the curves QTT(tau) - ATT with pointwise and uniform bands and the p-value of a sup-t test that QTT(tau) = ATT at every quantile (no distributional effect beyond a location shift). Overlaying a separately estimated ATT on a QTT band is not a valid test of this, since it ignores the estimation error in the ATT and its correlation with the QTT. summary() reports the ATTs and the tests, autoplot() draws the overall ATT on the QTT curve, and autoplot(type = "qtt_minus_att") plots the difference with its band.

  • Aggregated QTTs (qtt_pte_aggregations()) are now exact (#25). The cells’ distribution functions used to be mixed on a 1,000-point grid of the pooled outcome, so each quantile was rounded up to a grid point, and quantile() on the mixture then rounded its jumps again. Weighted data and the equivalent row-replicated data gave different QTTs. The mixture now uses every support point of the cells’ CDFs (one sort), at about the same cost, through BMisc::combine_ecdfs(), which computes mixtures exactly in BMisc 1.4.11 (now required). Reported QTTs change slightly (on mpdta, by up to about 0.01). The cells’ F0/F1 must be step-function CDFs, as those from BMisc::weighted_ecdf() are. Bootstrap draws no longer keep their own overall CDFs, so memory does not grow with sample size times biters. The quantile of the treatment effect (qott_pte_aggregations()) is now exact in the same way. Its grid, 1,000 points on [-max(y), max(y)], also missed effects below -max(y), and ran backwards when every outcome was negative. Each cell’s QOTT is now its exact quantile too.

  • The doubly robust estimator is now est_method = "aipw" (augmented inverse probability weighting), the new default in pte_default(), pte_attgt() and did_rcs_attgt() (#30). "dr" still works as a deprecated alias, with a warning; it was ambiguous next to qte’s cond_dist = "dr" (distribution regression). An unsupported est_method now gives a clear error up front.

  • New control_group = "eventuallytreated" (#29): the comparison units are units that are treated at some point but not yet treated (net of anticipation) in either period of a group-time comparison, i.e. the not-yet-treated units other than the never treated. The latest-treated cohort then serves only as a comparison group, and periods from its treatment date on are dropped, as without a never-treated group. Units first treated after the last period count as eventually treated.

  • QTT results (pte_qtt), e.g. from qte’s estimators (#26):

    • summary() now returns a summary.pte_qtt object instead of printing, so the table no longer appears twice at the console;
    • the summary shows the dynamic (event-study) and group QTTs at selected quantiles (probs, default the median), not only the overall curve;
    • it labels the band (simultaneous over quantiles, or pointwise) and marks estimates whose band excludes 0 with *, like the ATT summary;
    • autoplot(type = "group") now plots each cohort’s QTT at the selected quantile(s); it used to error.

  • setup_pte() gains require_comparison (default TRUE). With FALSE, setup does not require comparison units and estimates every group; this is for estimators that use only variation within each group and build their own cells, such as contdid’s ACRT when no unit is untreated (contdid #5). process_dose_gt() then reports only ACRT results; ATT(d) and the overall ATT are NA.

  • control_group is now checked: it must be "notyettreated", "nevertreated" or "eventuallytreated". Any other value, including a typo, used to be treated as "nevertreated" without a warning.

  • Fixed designs without a never-treated group. setup_pte() (and setup_pte_basic()) removed the smallest group value assuming it was 0, so without never-treated units the earliest cohort was silently dropped and estimation could then fail. Now, as in did::att_gt(), the latest cohort serves as the comparison group (as never treated with control_group = "nevertreated", with a warning) and periods from its treatment date on are dropped. If every unit is treated in the same period, there is now a clear error that no comparison units exist.

  • Fixed the empirical-bootstrap aggregation with weightsname: cohorts were combined by unweighted unit counts instead of weighted shares, so overall and event-study results were wrong whenever average weights differed across cohorts (#23). This affected estimators that use the empirical bootstrap, including qte’s. They now match pte_aggte().

  • Sampling weights are now checked (#24): they must be non-missing, finite and non-negative with a positive sum, and, with panel data, constant over time within each unit (as in did). Previously, invalid weights gave NaN estimates or inconsistent results without an error.

  • Empirical bootstrap: group effects and event times of a small cohort that is missing from some bootstrap draws now keep their estimates and get standard errors from the draws that contain the cohort; if it is missing from more than 10% of the draws, the standard errors are NA (#22). Before, such estimates were dropped from the results, estimate and all, if any single draw missed the cohort. The same applies to the QTT estimators. Also fixed: group-time standard errors from the empirical bootstrap were attached to the wrong (g,t) cells; they are now matched by group and time period.

  • New clustervars argument for pte_default(), pte() (via setup_pte()) to cluster standard errors at a level above the unit, as in did::att_gt() (#6): one variable, constant within each unit. It applies to analytical standard errors (cluster-robust variance, including the pre-test), the multiplier bootstrap (one multiplier per cluster, applied to influence functions summed within clusters) and the empirical bootstrap (whole clusters are resampled), for group-time effects and all aggregations. mboot2() and getSE() gain a cluster argument. Unclustered results are unchanged.

  • setup_pte() now stores control_group in the pte_params object, so later steps (the overall ATT for continuous treatments) use the requested comparison group instead of always the default. Continuous-treatment results (process_dose_gt()) now work with base_period = "universal".

  • Covariate formulas can now transform variables, e.g. xformula = ~ factor(state) + I(x^2) + log(z), in pte_default() / pte_attgt(), did_attgt() and covid_attgt() (#5). Such terms failed with “object not found”. Results for untransformed covariates are unchanged.

  • An error while estimating one group-time cell now says which group and time period it is (in units of tname) (#17). With a continuous treatment, a cohort with no more treated units than parameters in the dose regression now gives a clear error instead of “something off with overall influence function”.

  • The empirical bootstrap no longer errors when a bootstrap draw contains no treated units, which happened often with small cohorts (#10). Such draws are dropped, with a warning that says how many, and standard errors use the remaining draws. This also applies to the QTT estimators in qte.

  • pte_default() with est_method = "dr" no longer warns “non-integer #successes in a binomial glm!” on every call (#20). The overlap check now fits its logit propensity score with quasibinomial() and weights normalized to mean 1; fitted values, and so results, are unchanged.

  • No more flood of warnings from the multiplier bootstrap with base_period = "universal" (#3). The sup-t critical value for uniform confidence bands is computed only when it is used (cband = TRUE), and only over parameters with a positive standard error, which leaves out the universal reference period (0 by construction). This removes one warning per bootstrap draw (“no non-missing arguments to max”) and spurious “critical value … somehow smaller” warnings. Results are unchanged. mboot2() gains a cband argument.

  • cl now parallelizes the empirical bootstrap on Windows too (#11). A numeric cl only worked by forking, which Windows does not support, so there the bootstrap silently ran serially. On Windows, ptetools now creates a cluster with cl workers (reproducible with set.seed()) and stops it afterwards. cl can also be a cluster object from parallel::makeCluster(), on any platform. The documentation of cl now says what it does.

  • The pre-test of parallel trends is now reported with base_period = "universal" (#18). The reference cells, which are 0 by construction, made the covariance matrix singular. Cells with zero variance are now left out, as in did::att_gt(), and the pre-test matches did for both base periods.

  • Fixed standard errors of aggregated parameters (overall ATT, event study, group effects) from pte_aggte(), which were slightly off (about 0.3-0.8% on mpdta) (#19). The term for estimating the group shares used shares normalized to sum to 1 across treated groups instead of P(G = g). They now match did::aggte() exactly. Point estimates are unchanged.

  • overall_weights() (used for continuous treatments) no longer stops with “something’s going wrong calculating overall weights” when the weights sum to 1 only up to floating-point rounding, which happened with many timing groups (#1).

  • The bstrap documentation no longer refers to dev/NOTES.md, which is not part of the package; it now says what happens with a continuous treatment (#4).

  • anticipation now follows did::att_gt(): it is measured in units of the time variable (e.g., years), not in number of periods, which matters when periods are not one unit apart. Specifically:

    • the base period is the last period at least anticipation before treatment, and cells with t >= g - anticipation are post-treatment;
    • not-yet-treated comparison units must not be anticipating treatment in either period of the cell (first treated more than anticipation after both periods), so units about to anticipate are no longer used as controls;
    • the pre-test leaves out anticipation periods;
    • units first treated more than anticipation after the last period are treated as never treated (previously an error);
    • a clear error is given when no group has a period early enough to serve as its base period.

    Results with anticipation = 0 are unchanged. With anticipation > 0, results can change even with consecutive periods, because of the comparison-group rule.

  • New exported helpers for custom subset functions: pte_base_period() gives the base period of a group-time cell as in did::att_gt(), and pte_calendar_time() maps internal period indices back to the time variable. two_by_two_subset() uses them.

  • Fixed pre-treatment ATT(g,t) with base_period = "universal" and not-yet-treated controls (the default) (#16). The comparison group could include units already treated in the base period, which comes after the current period in pre-treatment cells. Not-yet-treated controls are now units first treated after both periods of the cell, as in did::att_gt(). Post-treatment estimates and the overall ATT are unchanged; pre-trends in event studies can change. pte_default() now matches did::att_gt() for both base periods and both control groups, including with unequally spaced time periods.

  • biters = 0 now skips the bootstrap (#14). It crashed the multiplier bootstrap, and earlier versions silently ran 2 bootstrap draws. Where attgt_fun returns an influence function, biters = 0 is the same as bstrap = FALSE (analytical, pointwise standard errors). Where standard errors are only available from the bootstrap (the empirical bootstrap, including the QTT estimators, and ATT(d)/ACRT(d) with a continuous treatment), the point estimates are returned with NA standard errors. biters must now be a non-negative whole number.

  • Fixed estimates when a column named in gname, tname, idname or yname is called G, period, id or Y (#13). With gname = "G" or tname = "period" and groups coded as calendar years, the overall ATT and event study were silently NaN. setup_pte() and setup_pte_basic() now store their internal columns as .G, .id, .period and .Y, and never modify the user’s columns.

  • Breaking change for custom setup and subset functions. The full data from a setup function now has the internal columns .G, .id, .period, .Y, .w and .rowid, not G, id, period and Y. Subset functions should select rows using the dot columns and finish with gt_data_frame(), which gives each group-time cell the columns G, id, period and Y (attgt_funs are unchanged). gt_data_frame() now errors if the dot columns are missing. keep_all_untreated_subset() and keep_all_pretreatment_subset() now also return gt_data_frame cells.

  • Fixed the standard errors of ATT(d) and ACRT(d) from process_dose_gt() (used by contdid) when dvals does not span exactly the range of the positive doses: the influence functions were built with a different B-spline basis than the one the dose regression was fitted with. process_dose_gt() now uses the boundary knots in ptep$boundary_knots when present, and otherwise keeps the previous behavior (#7; thanks to @AsadGudzevic94).

  • Fixed pte_attgt(), did_attgt() and covid_attgt() (and so pte_default()) giving wrong estimates with covariates or sampling weights when the data were not sorted by id within each period: covariates and weights were paired with other units’ outcomes (#9). setup_pte() now sorts panel data by id and period, and the 2x2 cells are matched by id. Results for data already sorted this way are unchanged.

  • pte() and pte_default() are faster, with the same results; the empirical bootstrap (used by the qte estimators) is often more than 10x faster. Speedups:

    • The bootstrap resamples units by index.
    • Each (g,t) cell is built from row indices computed once.
    • pte_default() keeps only the columns it uses.
    • The multiplier bootstrap is vectorized and uses the same random draws as before.
    • data.table is no longer a dependency.

  • The multiplier-bootstrap standard errors for ATT(g,t) now use biters draws. Previously they always used 1000 draws, whatever biters was set to. Aggregated parameters already used biters.

  • setup_pte() now gives a clear error when a value of gname is neither 0 nor one of the time periods.

  • Fixed standard errors for aggregated parameters (overall ATT, event study) when weightsname is used: they depended on the scale of the weights and were far too large for weights not near 1, such as population counts (#8). Weights are now normalized to mean 1 before aggregation, as in did. Point estimates are unchanged.

  • Added bstrap argument to pte(), pte_default(), setup_pte(), and setup_pte_basic() to request purely analytical (non-bootstrap) standard errors (bstrap = FALSE) instead of the multiplier bootstrap, wherever attgt_fun returns an influence function. This skips the (often expensive) multiplier bootstrap entirely and is much faster for large panels. bstrap = FALSE only supports pointwise confidence intervals (falls back from cband = TRUE with a warning), overrides boot_type = "empirical", and is not currently supported for continuous treatment (gt_type = "dose").

  • Fixed a bug in crit_val_checks() that threw object 'dp' not found when a simultaneous critical value could not be computed (e.g. designs with no pre-treatment periods, where standard errors come back NA). The fallback to pointwise critical values now works correctly, and pte()/process_dose_gt() correctly downgrade their cband flag so summary() reports “Pointwise” rather than “Simult.” whenever this fallback occurs.

  • Fixed a bug where autoplot.dose_obj() (used by contdid::ggcont_did()) crashed with arguments imply differing number of rows because the critical value stored on dose_obj carried a stray "cband" attribute left over from crit_val_checks(), which broke data.frame() recycling.

ptetools 1.0.1

CRAN release: 2026-07-20

  • Force time periods to be positive integers in ptetools::setup_pte()

  • Fix bug related to accounting for variance of untreated group with continuous treatment

  • Added covid_data dataset (previously in ppe); updated GitHub Actions workflows; fixed several documentation issues; dropped tidyr dependency in favour of data.table

  • Added pte_default(), a convenience wrapper combining setup_pte(), two_by_two_subset(), and pte_attgt() for standard DID/unconfoundedness-style estimation

  • Added support for repeated cross-sectional data via panel = FALSE, with a new two_by_two_rcs_subset() subset function

  • Added print(), summary(), autoplot(), and plot() methods for pte_emp_boot (empirical bootstrap results)

  • Added aggte_fun argument to pte(), panel_empirical_bootstrap(), and qtt_empirical_bootstrap() for supplying a custom group-time aggregation function on the empirical bootstrap path

  • Bumped minimum required BMisc version to 1.4.8 — ptetools calls several BMisc functions (add_cov_to_formula, rhs_vars, combine_ecdfs, get_list_element, weighted_combine_list) that were not available until that version

ptetools 1.0.0

CRAN release: 2025-02-13

  • Initial CRAN submission.
